predecessors.name: Stem Duchy of Swabia
predecessors.text: the Breisgau around Freiburg and Breisach

successors.name: Holy Roman Empire
successors.text: Zürich and Schaffhausen, partly reverted to the crown or granted imperial immediacy

successors.name: County of Urach
successors.text: the Breisgau around Freiburg and Breisach

ledger.x: 1098: Berthold II becomes Duke of Zähringen.
1098: the Zähringer receive jurisdiction over Zürich.
1127: Conrad is made rector of Burgundy.
1156: the lands south of Lake Geneva go to Savoy and Provence.
1173: the Zähringer acquire Zürich after the Lenzburg extinction ('Zürich was acquired' in 1173).
1173: Berthold IV acquires Zürich after the Lenzburg line dies out; the Zähringer already held the imperial advocacy.
1198: Philip pays Berthold V 3,000 silver marks for renouncing his claim to the throne.
1218: the Burgundian Rectorate ends with the dukes.
1218: Berthold V dies in Freiburg and the ducal line ends.

wars.name: Zähringen contest for Swabia
wars.outcome: Berthold II was elected duke of Swabia in 1092 against Frederick I; the Breisgau was ceded in 1096 and in 1098 he renounced Swabia and became Duke of Zähringen.

wars.name: Uprising of the Burgundian nobles (1198)
wars.outcome: Berthold V crushed an uprising of the Burgundian nobles in 1198.

wars.name: Battle of Ulrichen
wars.outcome: Berthold V failed to gain access to the Valais at Ulrichen in 1211 and had to accept Savoyard suzerainty over the upper Valais by the treaty of Hautcret Abbey on 19 October 1211.

certainty.note: No page gives a border; the Breisgau, Ortenau and Burgundian lands are approximated by circles and cantons.
